cues.zh: 最初的抱负很简单：这个国家能做些什么来创造就业、发展经济，好养活人民？
cues.en: The ambition was simply, what can the country do to generate jobs, to generate, um, economy to feed the people?

cues.zh: 本质上，这其实是一个非常朴素的意图。
cues.en: Essentially it was a very actually modest intention.

cues.zh: 在计划经济下，有一套社会保障网。
cues.en: Under the planned economy, there was a, a social safety net.

cues.zh: 每个人按配额领取粮票、布票和电票。
cues.en: Every person was rationed with food coupons, clothing coupons, electricity coupons.

cues.zh: 只有在深圳，你才能用钱买到一块面包，人们才愿意来深圳这个经济特区。
cues.en: It was only in Shenzhen you can buy a piece of bread with money, to be willing to come to Shenzhen to the special economic zone.

cues.zh: 去尝试创造些别的东西。
cues.en: To try to create something else.

cues.zh: 它吸引了那些想要更多自由的人。
cues.en: It attracted people who wanted to have more freedom.

cues.zh: 对我来说，深圳的非凡之处在于
cues.en: What to me was remarkable about Shenzhen is that

cues.zh: 就连规划者自己也会告诉你，这座城市的发展规模比他们预想的更大、速度也更快。
cues.en: even the planners themselves would tell you that the city evolved in a way much bigger and faster than they would have predicted.

cues.zh: 我认为，说深圳原本一无所有，然后设立经济特区，突然就变成一座城市，这种说法过于笼统了。
cues.en: I think it's it's overly generalized to saying that Shenzhen was nothing and then with a setup special economic zone, suddenly it became a city.

cues.zh: 但它没有。
cues.en: It didn't.

cues.zh: 还有些问题，单靠自上而下的规划是回答不了的。
cues.en: There is something else that's not answered simply by top down planning.

cues.zh: 大家早上好。感谢各位来和我一起讨论正在中国发生的创新。
cues.en: Yes, so good morning. Thank you all for joining me in a discussion about innovation that is happening right here in China.

cues.zh: 我们正与你们开发者社区共同投入。
cues.en: We're investing with you the developer community.

cues.zh: 我们一直在投资开源方案，因为我们知道，有了标准、有了开源产品，技术创新和技术普及的速度就会加快。
cues.en: We have been investing in open source solutions because we know that when there are standards, and when there are open source offerings, that the pace of technology innovation and the pace of technology adoption accelerates.

cues.zh: 我认为过去100年，工业革命把我们关进了小笼子。
cues.en: I think for the past 100 years, the industrial revolution put us into small cages.

cues.zh: 消费主义让大量创造力排队搁置。
cues.en: Consumerism has queued a lot of creativity.

cues.zh: 但对后工业世代来说，他们应该有更多自由去创造、探索和发明。
cues.en: But for the post industrial generation, they should have more freedom to create, to explore, to invent.

cues.zh: 我觉得，通过创客运动，我们正在把它带回来。
cues.en: I think through maker movement we are bringing it back.

cues.zh: 我这儿有 MakerBot，呃，Cupcake CNC，这是一台 3D 打印机。
cues.en: So I'm here with the MakerBot, uh, Cupcake CNC, which is a 3D printer.

cues.zh: 你可以制作 Tom York 的头之类的东西，因为他其实把自己一个视频的拍摄数据开源了。
cues.en: You can build things like Tom York's head, because he actually open sourced the data that was filmed uh for a video of his.

cues.zh: 整个场景还有意思的一点是，有一个非常活跃的用户社区。
cues.en: Now what's also interesting about this whole scenario is that there's a whole thriving community of users.

cues.zh: 他们用这些设备制作各种不同的东西。
cues.en: who are taking these to build all kinds of different objects.

cues.zh: 他们在网上分享这些物品。
cues.en: They're sharing the objects online.

cues.zh: 此外，他们还分享如何制作并改进设计的信息。
cues.en: In additionally, they're sharing information on how to build and improve upon the design.

cues.zh: 一切都是完全开源的，软件是开源的。
cues.en: Everything is completely open sourced, the software is open source.

cues.zh: 硬件也是开源的。
cues.en: The hardware is open source.

cues.zh: 我迫不及待想看看人们会做出什么。
cues.en: I just can't wait to see what people come up with.

cues.zh: 我认为，最近兴起的创客运动大概始于 2003、2004 年的美国。
cues.en: I think the recent emerging of the maker movement pretty much started around 2003, 2004 in the US.

cues.zh: 激光切割和 3D 打印。
cues.en: Laser cutting and 3D printing.

cues.zh: 它正帮助人们能够动手做东西，并且真正为了好玩去做，而不只是出于商业目的。
cues.en: is helping people to be able to build stuff and actually build it for fun, rather than just having business purpose.

cues.zh: 大约就在那时，一个叫 Dale Dougherty 的人正想着创办一本叫 Make 的刊物。
cues.en: Right around that time a guy named Dale Dougherty, he was thinking about starting a publication called Make.

cues.zh: 在 Make 问世之前，
cues.en: Before Make came out,

cues.zh: 我们唯一有的词就是黑客，对吧？
cues.en: the only word we had was a hacker, right?

cues.zh: 我觉得他不想把杂志叫 Hack，因为当时这个词有很强的负面含义。
cues.en: And I think he didn't want to call the magazine Hack because it had a really negative connotation at the time.

cues.zh: 而 Make 有点像你编译程序时会输入的东西，所以很容易引起程序员的共鸣。
cues.en: And Make was sort of the thing you would type to compile a program, so it would resonate well with with programmers.

cues.zh: 而“创客”大致就是会读这本杂志的那类人的称谓。
cues.en: And a maker was like sort of the demonym of people who would read the magazine.

cues.zh: 这大致创造了“创客”这个词。
cues.en: That sort of coined the term maker.

cues.zh: 我觉得通过创办那本刊物，他某种程度上把这个运动稳固下来了。
cues.en: I think in creating that publication, he sort of solidified the movement.

cues.zh: 而 Maker Faire 造就了这一现象。
cues.en: And the Maker Faire created that phenomenon.

cues.zh: 在中国，一开始没人了解创客。
cues.en: In China, in the beginning, nobody knows about makers.

cues.zh: 没人关心创客，但因为我们去过纽约和湾区的 Maker Faire，我们特别羡慕。
cues.en: Nobody cared about maker, but because we go to the Maker Faire in New York, in Bay Area, we are so jealous.

cues.zh: 所以，与其等别人来做，我们说，为什么不由我们来做？
cues.en: So, instead of waiting for someone to do it, we say, why don't we do it?

cues.zh: 当他们告诉我，要把第一届 Maker Faire 带到这里时，
cues.en: When they told me they were going to bring the first Maker Faire here,

cues.zh: 我当时就想，在一个人们不把动手制作当消遣、而是当工作的地方，你们怎么搞 Maker Faire？
cues.en: I was like, how do you have a Maker Faire in an area where people don't make for a recreational thing, they do it for a job?

cues.zh: 对吧？你知道，在西方，动手制作是用来提醒服务型经济里的人：还有制造业这回事，对吧？
cues.en: Right? You know, cuz making in the West is something that you're using to remind people who are in service economies, that there's a thing called manufacturing, right?

cues.zh: 当你身处制造业经济，却还要提醒他们还有制造业，这看起来很奇怪。
cues.en: When you have a manufacturing economy, you want to remind them there's manufacturing, it seems weird.

cues.zh: 我意识到，中国中产阶级的规模相当于整个美国的人口。
cues.en: And what I realized is that actually China's middle class is the size of the entire United States population.

cues.zh: 所以，哪怕只有一小部分中国人步入中上阶层，相较于美国的制造规模，这也足以在中国本土催生一场运动。
cues.en: So even if a small section of Chinese people had risen to the upper middle class, it's big enough to create a movement in China itself compared to the United States scale of making.

cues.zh: 我们不知道它会不会成功。
cues.en: We don't know if it's going to be successful or not.

cues.zh: 第一年我们有六十多位创客，
cues.en: The first year we have over 60 makers,

cues.zh: 去年我们有超过两百位创客。
cues.en: and last year we have over 200 makers.

cues.zh: 这是个很大的数字。
cues.en: It's a huge number.

cues.zh: 过去几年里，也涌现出一些有趣的现象。
cues.en: Some interesting phenomena also emerging out of this in the past years.

cues.zh: 正在发生的是开源硬件运动。
cues.en: What's happening is the open source hardware movement.

cues.zh: 传统上，电路板是闭源、专有的。
cues.en: Traditionally the circuit board is closed and proprietary.

cues.zh: 你得签合同、签保密协议，还要付一大笔预付款，才能拿到使用权。
cues.en: You need to have a contract, a non disclosure and a huge sum of prepayment in order to get access.

cues.zh: 但有了开源硬件，每个人都能获取这些信息，也都能按自己的需求修改。
cues.en: But with open source hardware, everybody can access to that information and everybody can modify that to suit their need.

cues.zh: 这里的人做出一块电路板，就是抱着这种预期。
cues.en: People here, they create a circuit board and just under expectation.

cues.zh: 它会被开源。
cues.en: It is going to be open.

cues.zh: 它会被别人复制并演进。
cues.en: It's going to be copied and evolved by someone else.

cues.zh: 在深圳，没人会到处说：行，这个是我做的，得给我记名。
cues.en: There's no one running around in Shenzhen and say, okay well, I should be credited for creating this.

cues.zh: 如果别人也能做出来，那就让别人去用它。
cues.en: If someone else can make this, get someone else to use it.

cues.zh: 越多越好。
cues.en: Merrier the better.

cues.zh: 不把自我绑在创作上，并且理解开源系统实际是怎么运作的。
cues.en: Not having the ego attached to creation, and understand how actually open source system works.

cues.zh: 呃，创客运动正处在那个节点上。
cues.en: Uh the maker movement is at that juncture.

cues.zh: 我有点听腻了电视上反复讲那几个人，一遍又一遍。
cues.en: I'm getting a little sick of hearing about the same people on TV, over and over and over again.

cues.zh: 所以我决定做点什么。
cues.en: So I decided to do something about it.

cues.zh: 这个 Arduino 项目，我把它叫“够了”，只要提到这些过度曝光的名人中的任何一个，它就会把电视静音。
cues.en: This Arduino project, which I call the enough already, will mute the TV anytime any of these over exposed personalities is mentioned.

cues.zh: 要把电视静音，我打算用一个红外 LED。
cues.en: To mute the TV, I'm going to use an IR LED.

cues.zh: 现在，只要提到某个关键词，电视就会静音 30 秒。
cues.en: Now, anytime a keyword is mentioned, the TV will mute for 30 seconds.

cues.zh: 我们的制片人今天早些时候采访了 Kim Kardashian。
cues.en: Our producers caught up with Kim Kardashian earlier today.

cues.zh: 它应该能很好地保护我们的耳朵，不用再听 Kim Kardashian 婚礼的那些细节了。
cues.en: It should do a pretty good job of protecting our ears from having to hear about the details of Kim Kardashian's wedding.

cues.zh: Arduino 正在成为一个触发点，
cues.en: Arduino is becoming the trigger point,

cues.zh: 因为有几百万创客在用。
cues.en: because it has so many millions of makers using that.

cues.zh: 这是他尝试做的一个原型。
cues.en: This is a prototype he tried to make.

cues.zh: 这条机械臂是给他们……嗯，患帕金森病的人做的。
cues.en: The robotic arm for their uh people have Parkinson diseases.

cues.zh: 我们想做一个……嗯，这样的勺子。
cues.en: We want to make a spoon, uh, like this.

cues.zh: 你只要……嗯，坐在这儿，对，很稳。
cues.en: And if you just uh sit here, and yeah. stable.

cues.zh: 如果我们回到 10 年前、20 年前的深圳，创客想获得资源会非常困难。
cues.en: If we come to Shenzhen like 10 years ago, 20 years ago, it will be very difficult for a maker to tap into resources.

cues.zh: 但现在你有这么多资源。
cues.en: But now you have so many resources.

cues.zh: 它正处于转型之中。
cues.en: It's in the middle of a reforming.

cues.zh: 所以大公司，尤其是呃，芯片供应商，比如 Intel、Atmel、TI，他们看到这个就说，哦，
cues.en: So the big company, especially the uh silicon providers, like Intel, like Atmel, like TI, they look at that, oh,

cues.zh: 我们有新客户了。
cues.en: We have new customers.

cues.zh: 我们的技术有了面向未来新应用的新可能。
cues.en: We have new possibility for a new future applications of our technologies.

cues.zh: 所以他们自己做控制器板，比如 Edison，比如 Curie。
cues.en: So they make their own controller board, like Edison, like Curie.

cues.zh: 所以他们想切入应用开发的进行阶段。
cues.en: So they they they want to tap into the running stage of the development of the applications.

cues.zh: 现在这块板基于 Intel 技术。
cues.en: Now this board is based on the Intel technology.

cues.zh: 它是一个微型双核计算机系统。
cues.en: It's a tiny dual core computer system.

cues.zh: 它有 Wi-Fi、蓝牙，而且上面还运行 Linux 操作系统。
cues.en: It has Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and it also it it runs a Linux operating system on it.

cues.zh: 我认为 Intel 不得不转向那种方式的部分原因是，
cues.en: I think part of the reason Intel is having to sort of turn that way,

cues.zh: 他们和其他任何人一样清楚自己的路线图。
cues.en: they know their roadmap as well as anyone else does.

cues.zh: 他们某种程度上定义了摩尔定律，也比其他人更早看到脚下的桥断了。
cues.en: They they kind of define Moore's Law, and they saw the bridge go out from underneath them before anyone else did.

cues.zh: 他们曾设法这样推动技术发展，然后
cues.en: They managed to drive technology like this and then

cues.zh: 像台积电和联电这样的其他代工厂，一直落在后面。
cues.en: the other foundries like TSMC and UMC have always trailed behind.

cues.zh: 但现在他们慢下来了，所有人都在追赶。
cues.en: But now they're slowing down, everyone's catching up.

cues.zh: 他们就像，天啊，我们在找空气，想找个地方挪一挪。
cues.en: They're like, oh God, we're looking for air and trying to find a place to move.

cues.zh: 所以，他们很难跟上自己创造出的现象。
cues.en: And so, they've struggled to keep up with the phenomenon they created.

cues.zh: 他们没能在移动领域取得进展，而移动设备是如今最普及的计算机。
cues.en: They haven't made headway into mobile, and those are the most ubiquitous computer today.

cues.zh: 他们正错失巨大的市场机会。
cues.en: They're missing out on a huge market opportunity.

cues.zh: 所以，他们正设法把创新模式调整得更灵活。
cues.en: And so to the extent that they're trying to figure out how to adapt their innovation model to something more flexible.

cues.zh: 所以他们真的很想确保 Intel 品牌出现在年轻人面前，让他们记住 Intel 其实是他们以后会想用来做设计的东西，
cues.en: And so they really want to make sure the Intel brand is in front of the youth, to make sure that they remember that Intel is actually like a thing that they want to design with later on,

cues.zh: 而不只是，你知道，遥不可及的东西。
cues.en: and not just, you know, something out of reach.

cues.zh: 我们试着把它介绍给 9 岁的孩子。
cues.en: We have tried to introduce it to 9 years old.

cues.zh: 这东西有点难，但还可以接受。
cues.en: This thing is a little bit difficult, but it's acceptable.

cues.zh: 你不需要写任何无聊的代码。
cues.en: You do not need to write any boring code.

cues.zh: 在智能笔记里，你只需拖放并把它们链接起来。
cues.en: In a smart note, you can just drag and drop and link them together.

cues.zh: 他们做的是学习如何在电脑上编程，把它转成硬件，然后用我们的激光切割机或 3D 打印机制作一个项目，让某个东西能接收刺激，
cues.en: What they're doing is they're learning how to code on a computer, translate that into hardware and they'll build a project on our laser cutter or 3D printer for something to accept a stimulus,

cues.zh: 比如光、运动或声音，然后输出某种结果。
cues.en: light, motion or sound, and then output some result.

cues.zh: 去年，有个孩子给他妈妈做了一个钥匙提醒器：她出门时，运动传感器会检测到她的移动，并说，嘿，别忘了钥匙。
cues.en: Last year, one kid built a key reminder for his mom, so that when she left the house, a motion sensor would pick up her movement and say, hey, don't forget the key.

cues.zh: 挺有趣的是，一个 8 岁孩子会知道自己是想做机械电路，还是只想做纯软件体验。
cues.en: And it's kind of funny to hear that an 8 year old will know whether he wants to be doing mechanical circuits or just a purely software experience.

cues.zh: 所以那是入门级别，然后我们会更系统地介绍如何逐步培养这些技能。
cues.en: So that that's enter level, and then we give them more systematic introduction how to build up the skills.

cues.zh: 去吧，你可以用创客空间创造任何你想要的东西。
cues.en: Off you go, you can use a maker space to create whatever you want.

cues.zh: 你们是天才，你们是年轻的发明家。
cues.en: You are genius, you are young inventors.

cues.zh: 我见过一些很好的例子，开源硬件被用来真正带来改变、创造更美好的世界。
cues.en: I've seen some great examples of open source hardware being used to actually make a difference and create a better world.

cues.zh: 难点在于如何把它变现。
cues.en: the difficulty is monetizing that.

cues.zh: 因为我确实相信商业能解决世界上的很多问题，而人们需要能够赚钱。
cues.en: Because I do believe that business solves a lot of the world's problems and people need to be able to make money.

cues.zh: 如果你在为世界提供价值，也就是让世界变得更好，那就应该得到回报。
cues.en: If you're providing value to the world, which is making the world a better place, then there should be compensation for that.

cues.zh: 2010年，我在中国创办了第一家创客空间，叫 XinCheJian。
cues.en: In 2010, I started the first maker space in China, called XinCheJian.

cues.zh: 我经常受邀去做关于开源硬件的演讲。
cues.en: I got invite a lot to give a talk about open source hardware.

cues.zh: 人们脑子里冒出来的第一个问题总是：你怎么保护自己的知识产权？如果不保护知识产权，又怎么赚钱呢？
cues.en: The first question always come out from people's mind is, well, how do you protect your intellectual property and how can you make money if you don't protect your intellectual property?

cues.zh: 我在上海被问到这个问题，在北京也被问到，走到哪儿都被问。但我在深圳做同样的演讲时，得到的反应却是：这有什么新鲜的？我们靠这个赚钱都赚了20年了。
cues.en: I got that question in Shanghai, I got that question in Beijing, I got that question everywhere I go, but when I give the same talk in Shenzhen, the reaction I got is, so what's new about this? We've been making money on this for 20 years.

cues.zh: 我们来深圳，完全就是因为这里的电子市场。
cues.en: The reason we're here in in Shenzhen is literally because of the electronics markets.

cues.zh: 那里有各种可能的元器件和各种设备，是个绝佳的资源库。
cues.en: You know, it's a fantastic resource of all different possible components and different devices.

cues.zh: 团队可以把它们像弗兰肯斯坦一样拼凑起来做原型。
cues.en: which can kind of be Frankenstein together to make prototypes by the teams.

cues.zh: 它是灵感的来源。
cues.en: It's a source of inspiration.

cues.zh: 这里是发现新产品的地方，这些产品有可能被带到西方市场。
cues.en: It's a source of discovery of new products that could potentially be taken to the West.

cues.zh: 我每个月都能在那里看到不同的新发明。
cues.en: And like I see every month a different invention down there.

cues.zh: 十有八九，它们进不了西方市场，但有些确实能成。
cues.en: 9 times out of 10, they're probably not going to make it to the West, but some of them do.
